description: Content-addressed execution trace for scientific reproducibility verification. Records the runtime provenance of a study execution so that paper-derived scientific contracts can be checked against what actually ran, not what the repository merely contains.
design_principles: Content-addressed: every entity carries a stable hash; outputs record upstream entities that contributed to them.
Existing standards where practical: aligns with W3C PROV concepts (Entity/Activity/Agent) and RO-Crate structure rather than inventing a new provenance model.
Execution-independent inputs must be identical across a paired execution: paper, repository, code_commit. Only runtime/execution fields may differ.
No gold label leakage: the trace must not encode which execution is clean vs. invalid; that is derived by the verifier against the contract.

run_id.description: Unique identifier for this execution (not necessarily stable across the pair).

code_commit.description: Full git SHA of the code that was executed. MUST be identical across paired clean/invalid executions (same code, different runtime behaviour).

environment_hash.description: Hash of the runtime environment (python version, key library versions, device). Identical across a pair.

config_hash.description: SHA256 of the raw config file(s) loaded at runtime. May differ between paired runs if the fault is a runtime config mismatch.

seed.description: Random seed for this single execution. In a seed-aggregation study, multiple runs each have their own seed; the trace records this run's seed.

protocol.description: The scientific protocol as declared/executed. This is where paper-derived contracts are checked.

declared_seeds.description: Seed population the paper declares (e.g. [0,1,2,3,4] for 5 seeds).

aggregation_rule.description: How multiple-seed results are aggregated into the reported value. Paper typically declares 'mean'; a violation uses 'best'.

aggregation_inputs.description: run_ids whose metrics feed into the aggregated reported value.

selection_split.description: Which data split was used to select the checkpoint. Paper must say 'validation' or 'none' (no selection).

selection_dataset_hash.description: Content hash of the dataset actually used for checkpoint selection.

final_test_split.description: Identifier/href of the split used for the final reported evaluation. MUST be disjoint from selection_split in a clean execution.

final_test_dataset_hash.description: Content hash of the dataset actually used for final evaluation.

declared_preprocess.description: Preprocessing pipeline the paper declares (normalisation, augmentation, etc.).

executed_preprocess.description: Preprocessing pipeline actually applied at runtime. May diverge from declared_preprocess in E05.

reported_subgroups.description: Subgroup labels actually reported. May be a subset of declared_subgroups in E04.

declared_subgroups.description: Subgroup labels the paper says are reported.

hyperparameters.description: All hyperparameters actually used at runtime (lr, batch_size, epochs, etc.). Keyed by name.

loss_identity.description: Concrete loss function actually used, e.g. 'CrossEntropyLoss', 'nn.MSELoss'.

training_budget.description: Compute/training budget actually consumed. Relevant for E06 asymmetry.

comparator_budgets.description: Training budgets for each compared method. E06 checks declared fairness relations.

disjoint_split_ids.description: True if train/validation/test sample IDs are verified disjoint.

candidates.description: All checkpoint IDs that were available for selection.

selected.description: Checkpoint ID actually used for reporting.

metrics.description: Metric name -> value, each traceable to an upstream run_id/checkpoint.

outputs.description: Reported outputs, each recording upstream entities that produced it.

parent_run.description: Parent run_id if this is a child (multi-seed) execution.

self_hash.description: SHA256 over the canonical serialisation of this trace object (excluding self_hash). Makes the trace content-addressed.

identifiability_note: Within a paired execution, code_commit, environment_hash, and the paper are held constant. Only runtime/execution fields (seed, checkpoint.selection_split, protocol.executed_preprocess, aggregation_inputs, reported_subgroups, training_budget) may differ between the clean and invalid members.
